findings.title: Setting HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND env var to any supported backend makes `import hypertools` crash
findings.description: backend.py _init_backend's env-var branch (lines 547-556) is doubly broken: (1) it indexes `backends.index(HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND)` -- the module GLOBAL, which is still None at this point -- instead of `env_backend`, so the index call raises ValueError whenever the user's env value IS in the candidate list (MacOSX/TkAgg/QtAgg/Qt5Agg/Qt4Agg/GTK4Agg/GTK3Agg/WXAgg, any case); and (2) even with the right name it builds `(backends[:i], *backends[i+1:])` -- the first slice is missing its `*` unpack, which would nest a tuple into the candidates. The ValueError propagates out of the except-branch, `working_backend` is never bound, and the trailing `finally` raises UnboundLocalError -- import of the whole package fails. The env var is real, semi-documented functionality: plot()'s mpl_backend docstring says 'Set the `$HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND` environment variable ... to override the backend used by auto', and the code comment directly above the bug reads '# TODO: document setting environment variable'. Values NOT in the list (e.g. Agg) skip the branch and work.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND=TkAgg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c 'import hypertools'
findings.expected: hypertools imports and prefers the user-specified backend (falling back with a warning if it cannot be used), per the mpl_backend docstring.
findings.actual:
File "hypertools/plot/backend.py", line 552, in _init_backend
    backends[: backends.index(HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND)],
ValueError: tuple.index(x): x not in tuple
...
  File "hypertools/plot/backend.py", line 691, in _init_backend
    HYPERTOOLS_BACKEND = HypertoolsBackend(working_backend).normalize()
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'working_backend' where it is not associated with a value

findings.title: plot() is a single 2,690-line function with ~70 parameters
findings.description: hypertools/plot/plot.py `plot` spans lines 138-2827 (2,690 lines: ~1,090 lines of docstring + ~1,600 lines of body) and takes 70 keyword parameters plus **kwargs. The body chains kwarg validation, MultiIndex expansion, the analyze pipeline, forecast computation, hue classification (5 sub-branches), morph resolution, interpolation, center/scale, backend dispatch, colorbar/legend fitting, save, and 4 different return shapes in one scope, with state threaded through ~30 locals (xform, raw_xform, multicolor_hue, morph_tags, surface_list, ...). It is the package's largest readability liability: understanding any one feature requires paging through all of it, and its sections are already individually commented as if they were functions. The comments are excellent, which mitigates but does not remove the problem.
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import ast
src = open('/Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/plot.py').read()
f = [n for n in ast.parse(src).body if getattr(n, 'name', '') == 'plot'][0]
print(f.end_lineno - f.lineno + 1, 'lines,', len(f.args.args) + len(f.args.kwonlyargs), 'params')
EOF
findings.expected: Cohesive stages factored into module-level helpers (as _build_colorbar_info/_resolve_animate_mode already are), keeping plot() an orchestrator.

findings.title: matplotlib_backend._draw is an 1,841-line function containing ~24 nested closures
findings.description: `_draw` (matplotlib_backend.py lines 341-2181) defines ~24 nested functions (dispatch_static, plot1D/2D/3D, annotate_plot, update_position, _sync_anim_labels, hide_labels, add_labels, distance, calcClosestDatapoint, annotate_plot_explore, onMouseMotion, plot_cube, plot_square, update_lines_parallel/_spin/_serial, update_morph, dispatch_animate, animate_plot3D (463 lines), update_lines_parallel_2d, update_lines_serial_2d, update_morph_2d, animate_plot2D (222 lines), _plot_possibly_split, _wants_trail x2) that communicate through closure captures of _draw's 40 parameters and through function ATTRIBUTES used as mutable frame state (`update_lines_parallel.planes`, `.surface_colls`, `update_lines_spin.meshes`, `annotate_plot_explore.clicked`) plus a module-level `global labels_and_points`. None of these closures is unit-testable in isolation, and the function-attribute state leaks across successive plots (the code itself guards for this: 'it may also still hold a PREVIOUS plot's labels'). Also uses `assert` for user-facing input validation at line 1999 ('Animations are only supported for 2-D or 3-D plots'), which disappears under python -O.
findings.repro:
python - <<'EOF'
import ast
src = open('/Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py').read()
f = [n for n in ast.parse(src).body if getattr(n, 'name', '') == '_draw'][0]
nested = [n.name for n in ast.walk(f) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name != '_draw']
print(f.end_lineno - f.lineno + 1, 'lines;', len(nested), 'nested defs')
EOF
findings.expected: Frame-update callbacks and the explore/label helpers as module-level functions taking explicit state (as the newer surface/density helpers _draw_density_2d/_shade_and_cull_3d already are).

Across backends, the morph sampling + default-color fallback `(0.2, 0.4, 0.8)` appears FOUR times (matplotlib_backend 1379-1383 and 1878-1882; plotly_backend 674-678 and 1975-1979). update_lines_parallel/update_lines_parallel_2d and update_morph/update_morph_2d are further 3D/2D twins. findings.title: Animated plotly morph runs the O(n^3) Hungarian matching twice per figure
findings.description: plotly_draw computes `sampled0, dup_masks0 = _morph.sample_and_match_clouds(clouds0, morph_samples=...)` (plotly_backend.py:672) with a comment claiming this is 'so the cube_scale block below can reuse the EXACT sampled0 arrays _add_animation's 'morph' branch will later draw' -- but _add_animation does NOT receive sampled0; it independently re-runs `sample_and_match_clouds(clouds, morph_samples=morph_samples)` (line 1973) on the same data. The two results only coincide because both use the default seed=0; the linear_sum_assignment cost is roughly O(n^3), so every animated plotly morph pays the matching cost twice, and the 'EXACT arrays' invariant is enforced by nothing but the shared default seed.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, hypertools.plot.morph as m
calls = []
orig = m.sample_and_match_clouds
m.sample_and_match_clouds = lambda *a, **k: (calls.append(1), orig(*a, **k))[1]
from hypertools.plot.plotly_backend import plotly_draw
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
plotly_draw([rng.normal(size=(30,3)), rng.normal(3,1,(30,3))], fmt=['.','.'],
            kwargs_list=[{},{}], animate='morph', duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
print('sample_and_match_clouds calls:', len(calls))
EOF
findings.expected: 1 call per figure (plotly_draw passes sampled0/dup_masks0 into _add_animation).
findings.actual: 2 calls per animated morph figure (code-read: plotly_backend.py:672 and plotly_backend.py:1973; the comment at 652-656 asserts reuse that does not happen)

findings.title: explore mode: onMouseMotion never updates its previous-index state (dead local assignment)
findings.description: matplotlib_backend.py onMouseMotion (lines 811-835) initializes `onMouseMotion.closestIndex_prev` once on the first event, then on later events assigns `closestIndex_prev = closestIndex` -- a LOCAL variable that is never read (pyflakes: "matplotlib_backend.py:835:17: local variable 'closestIndex_prev' is assigned to but never used"); the function ATTRIBUTE is never updated. Consequence (from code): after the mouse leaves the initial closest point, every subsequent motion event with closestIndex != the FIRST-ever index re-runs annotate_plot_explore (redundant redraw per event), and moving back exactly onto the first point's region draws nothing. Not runtime-tested (requires live GUI mouse events; explore is documented as experimental) -- static evidence only. Related smell: `distance()` (line 739) uses `plt.gca().get_proj()` while the same function uses the closed-over `ax.transData` two lines later, so a different active axes would silently mix projections.
findings.repro: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -m pyflakes /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py | grep closestIndex
findings.expected: onMouseMotion.closestIndex_prev = closestIndex (attribute update), so the hover label re-renders exactly when the closest point changes.
findings.actual: hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py:835:17: local variable 'closestIndex_prev' is assigned to but never used (same dead assignment at line 832)

findings.title: plot() mutates the caller's fmt list in place (single-point line fmt rewritten to '.')
findings.description: plot.py line 2510-2512 aliases the user's list (`draw_fmt = fmt`, no copy) and matplotlib_backend._draw lines 1983-1985 then rewrite entries in place (`fmt[i] = '.'` for any single-point dataset whose fmt is '-', ':' or '--'). The caller's own list object is silently modified -- verified: a user list ['-', '-'] becomes ['.', '-'] after the call, so reusing the same fmt list for a second plot draws different styles.

import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
user_fmt = ['-', '-']
hyp.plot([np.array([[0.5, 0.5, 0.5]]), np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(5).normal(size=(10, 3)), axis=0)], user_fmt, show=False)
print(user_fmt)
EOF

findings.title: Animated trail artists ignore the user's linewidth= (destructive dict.pop in artist-creation comprehensions)
findings.description: In animate_plot3D/animate_plot2D the head-line comprehension calls `kwargs_list[idx].pop('linewidth', 1)` (matplotlib_backend.py:1303 etc.), destructively removing the key from the shared per-dataset dict; the trail comprehension that runs NEXT pops the now-missing key and falls back to 1. Verified: hyp.plot(traj, animate=True, chemtrails=True, linewidth=5) yields artist linewidths [5.0, 1.0] -- the faint trail renders at default width while the head honors 5. The same pop-mutation idiom is repeated 8 times across the two functions (see finding 004).
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
traj = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(6).normal(size=(30, 3)), axis=0)
fig, ani = hyp.plot(traj, animate=True, chemtrails=True, linewidth=5, duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
print([l.get_linewidth() for l in fig.axes[0].lines])
EOF
findings.expected: [5.0, 5.0] (trail mirrors the head's linewidth, differing only in alpha=0.3)

findings.title: azim= starting angle ignored by animate='parallel'/'spin' but honored by 'serial'/'morph' and by every plotly style
findings.description: update_lines_parallel (matplotlib_backend.py:966) and update_lines_spin (:1040) compute `azim_now = rotations * 360 * frac` -- dropping the user's/default `azim` offset -- while update_lines_serial (:1080) computes `azim + rotations * 360 * frac` and morph threads azim through morph_schedule. The plotly backend adds `azim` in ALL styles (plotly_backend.py:1926, :2065, :2164). So an animate=True or 'spin' matplotlib animation starts at azimuth 0 instead of the requested/default -60, differing both from its own 'serial'/'morph' siblings and from the plotly rendering of the identical call (first frame rotated 60 degrees apart). Verified by driving frame 0 of each style with azim=-60: {'parallel': 0.0, 'spin': 0.0, 'serial': -60.0}.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
traj = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(7).normal(size=(30, 3)), axis=0)
for style in ('parallel', 'spin', 'serial'):
    fig, ani = hyp.plot(traj, animate=style, duration=1, frame_rate=5, azim=-60, show=False)
    ani._init_draw(); ani._draw_frame(0)
    print(style, fig.axes[0].azim)
EOF
findings.expected: All styles (and both backends) start the camera at the requested azim (-60), as 'serial'/'morph'/plotly already do.

findings.title: plot() density docstring documents plotly Volume constants two retunes out of date
findings.description: plot.py's density docstring (lines 1168-1170) says plotly's 3-D layer uses "`opacity=min(3.0 * alpha, 0.6)`, a fixed `opacityscale` ramp". The shipped code (density.resolve_plotly_volume_params) uses `base_opacity = min(2.0 * alpha, 0.4)`, a BOOST-DEPENDENT opacityscale, and a MAX_VOLUME_OPACITY cap of 0.75; density.py's own docstrings explicitly describe the old min(3*alpha, 0.6) values as "lowered from the original" (R2 maintainer retune). Verified by running resolve_plotly_volume_params(0.2, 3, 1.0): opacity=0.4 vs the docstring's implied 0.6. (The 2-D claim '1.5 * alpha' IS accurate -- plotly_backend.py:1410.)
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "from hypertools.plot.density import resolve_plotly_volume_params; print(resolve_plotly_volume_params(0.2, 3, 1.0))"
findings.expected: Docstring matches code: opacity=min(2*alpha, 0.4) at boost=1, boost-scaled opacityscale, MAX_VOLUME_OPACITY=0.75 ceiling.

findings.title: plot() surface docstring says containment rescale 'grow at most 10%'; the code cap is 3.0x
findings.description: plot.py surface pre_inflate bullet (lines 1081-1085): 'Any shrinkage smoothing introduces is instead recovered by a minimal, mathematically bounded (grow at most 10%) post-hoc rescale'. meshutil.py sets `_RESCALE_CAP = 3.0` (grow up to 200%), with a long docstring in _rescale_for_containment explaining precisely why a ~1.1 cap would be WRONG ('A hard 1.1 cap would silently regress that long-standing guarantee... a bare (degenerate) 4-point tetrahedron needs ~2.9x'). The plot.py docstring predates that fix and now contradicts both the code and meshutil's own rationale.

findings.title: Stale pre-1.0 references: four comments cite 'draw.py' for code now in matplotlib_backend.py; backend.py docstring cites removed DataGeometry.plot and misnames functions
findings.description: draw.py is a documented 3-line rename shim ('Renamed to hypertools.plot.matplotlib_backend (HyperTools 1.0)'), but plotly_backend.py still points readers at it as if it held code: line 206 "(see draw.py's set_box_aspect conversion)", line 1141 "Mirrors draw.py's plot_cube", line 1168 "(mirrors draw.py's plot_square)", line 2162 "(draw.py update_lines_parallel)" -- all four functions live in matplotlib_backend.py (plot_cube/plot_square/update_lines_parallel are closures inside _draw; the zoom mapping is _anim_box_zoom). Separately, backend.py's module docstring (line 3-4) says the module manages the backend for plots 'created via hypertools.plot and hypertools.DataGeometry.plot' -- datageometry.py has no plot method in 1.0 (unpickle-only shell per its own docstring); line 51 misspells the decorator as 'manage_backed'; and lines 61-69 describe `switch_backend`/`reset_backend` as 'matplotlib.pyplot.switch_backend' (actually the wrapper `_switch_backend_regular`) and name '`_switch_notebook_backend`' (actual function: `_switch_backend_notebook`).
findings.repro: grep -n "draw.py" /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/plotly_backend.py; grep -n 'DataGeometry.plot\|manage_backed\|_switch_notebook_backend' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/backend.py; grep -n 'def plot' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/datageometry.py
findings.expected: Comments name the module/function that actually holds the code; backend.py docstring reflects the 1.0 API (no DataGeometry.plot) and the real function names.
findings.actual: plotly_backend.py:206,1141,1168,2162 reference draw.py; backend.py:4 references hypertools.DataGeometry.plot (grep for 'def plot' in datageometry.py returns nothing); backend.py:51 'manage_backed'; backend.py:68 '_switch_notebook_backend'

findings.title: set_interactive_backend docstring examples hardcode 'TkAgg' and crash on Pythons built without tkinter (infra-sensitive example)
findings.description: Both usage examples in backend.py's set_interactive_backend docstring (lines 936-956) use hyp.set_interactive_backend('TkAgg') + hyp.plot(data, interactive=True). Run VERBATIM on this repo's own .venv (a uv/pyenv-style CPython with no _tkinter -- common on macOS/Linux), example 1 raises HypertoolsBackendError at the second plot call ('Failed to switch the plotting backend to TkAgg. You may be missing required dependencies...'). The mechanism itself is fine -- the identical call with an installed backend ('MacOSX') succeeds -- so the canonical example is what fails. Tagged infra: whether it crashes depends on the host's Tk availability, but a doc example should use a portable pattern (e.g. mention checking matplotlib.rcsetup.interactive_bk, or use the render-backend form set_interactive_backend('plotly') that 1.0 added).
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jmanning-hypertools/7e6531b3-066a-4ce2-b1f6-7c07c5e87b15/scratchpad/audit/X6-code-org-plot/backend_docstring_example.py
findings.expected: Docstring examples run on a stock install of the package's own dev venv.
findings.actual: hypertools.core.exceptions.HypertoolsBackendError: Failed to switch the plotting backend to TkAgg. You may be missing required dependencies, or this backend may not be available for your system  (root cause: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_tkinter')

findings.title: Unused imports and dead locals (pyflakes-confirmed) across 6 modules
findings.description: pyflakes over the package: __init__.py:2-3 `warnings` and `matplotlib as mpl` unused; animate.py:11 module-level `combine_frames_svg` unused (shadowed by the local re-import at line 88 -- pyflakes flags the redefinition); plot.py:4 `matplotlib.animation` unused, plot.py:17 `_SVGFrameCollector`/`_save_animated_svg` imported but never used (nothing imports them FROM plot.py either -- grep-verified); matplotlib_backend.py:7 `matplotlib` unused; backend.py:480 local `lab_version_stdout` assigned but never read (only the retcode is used, unlike the parallel notebook_version_stdout block that reads its buffer); colors.py:167 re-exports `vals2colors`/`vals2bins` 'so plot.colors is the single coloring surface' but no module or test imports them from plot.colors (grep-verified) -- an aspirational re-export at the bottom of the file.

findings.expected: No unused imports/locals, or a noqa with a reason where a re-export is intentional.

findings.title: Star imports make load-bearing names invisible in the two biggest modules
findings.description: plot.py:7 and matplotlib_backend.py:13 both do `from .._shared.helpers import *`. Critical names -- np, itertools, reshape_data, parse_kwargs, is_line, has_line_component, interp_array(_list), patch_lines, group_by_category, vals2bins, split_marker_line_fmt -- arrive invisibly: pyflakes emits 60+ "'np' may be undefined, or defined from star imports" warnings and cannot check these files; plot.py uses `itertools` (lines 2098, 3287) and `np` throughout without importing either directly, so readers must know _shared.helpers re-exports whole modules. This hides the dependency surface of the package's two largest files and defeats linting.
findings.repro: /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -m pyflakes /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/plot.py /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py | grep -c 'star imports'
findings.expected: Explicit imports (import numpy as np, import itertools, from .._shared.helpers import reshape_data, ...), as plotly_backend.py already does.
findings.actual: 60 'may be undefined, or defined from star imports' pyflakes lines across the two files

findings.title: Naming inconsistencies: camelCase explore helpers, a 'tail_duration' parameter that receives frame counts, and '_3d' names reused for 2-D
findings.description: (1) The explore-mode closures in matplotlib_backend use camelCase against the package's otherwise-uniform snake_case: `calcClosestDatapoint`, `onMouseMotion`, `closestIndex`, `closestIndex_prev` (lines 746, 811, 821, 827). (2) `update_lines_parallel`'s parameter is named `tail_duration` (line 938) but every caller passes `window_frames` -- an int FRAME COUNT (frame_rate * seconds, matplotlib_backend.py:1601/1614) -- so `data[0 : num - tail_duration + 1]` reads as seconds arithmetic but is frames; the sibling plotly code names the same quantity `window`. (3) plotly_backend deliberately keeps `_3d`-suffixed locals (`morph_indices_3d`, `sampled0`... `morph_trace_start_3d`) for values now also used in 2-D, acknowledged in-code ('names keep their historical "_3d" suffix ... to minimize the diff', lines 658-661). (4) plot_cube(scale) uses the closed-over ax while its sibling plot_square(ax, scale) takes ax explicitly.
findings.repro: grep -n 'def calcClosestDatapoint\|def onMouseMotion\|def update_lines_parallel(\|morph_trace_start_3d' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/matplotlib_backend.py /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/plotly_backend.py
findings.expected: snake_case throughout; the frame-count parameter named window_frames; dimension-neutral names for dimension-neutral values.
findings.actual: matplotlib_backend.py:746 def calcClosestDatapoint; :811 def onMouseMotion; :932 def update_lines_parallel( with tail_duration=2 receiving window_frames; plotly_backend.py:756 morph_trace_start_3d used for 2-D too

findings.title: Missing module docstrings in the package's two largest files and __init__.py
findings.description: plot.py (3,332 lines) and matplotlib_backend.py (2,181 lines) have no module docstring at all (shebang + imports only), and plot/__init__.py (which runs _init_backend() at import time -- a side effect worth documenting) has none either. Every other module in the package carries a good module docstring (plotly_backend, backend, meshutil, morph, density, surface, fonts, multiindex, trails, animate, hyper_animation, colors); draw.py/interactive.py use a one-line `#` comment that does state their shim status. The two undocumented files are exactly the ones a new contributor needs orientation for most.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import ast
for f in ('plot.py', 'matplotlib_backend.py', '__init__.py'):
    src = open(f'/Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/{f}').read()
    print(f, ast.get_docstring(ast.parse(src)) is not None)
EOF
findings.expected: Module docstrings present (matching the standard set by plotly_backend.py's).

findings.title: Vestigial code fragments: dead conditional in _colorbar_trace and a duplicated TkAgg fallback entry
findings.description: (1) plotly_backend.py:1694: `thickness=15 if orientation == 'v' else 15` -- both branches identical; either a leftover from a removed asymmetric value or noise. (2) backend.py:530-539: the non-notebook fallback tuple lists "TkAgg" TWICE -- backends = ("TkAgg", "QtAgg", "Qt5Agg", "Qt4Agg", "GTK4Agg", "GTK3Agg", "TkAgg", "WXAgg") -- so a failing TkAgg import is attempted twice on every non-notebook import of hypertools.
findings.repro: grep -n "thickness=15 if" /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/plotly_backend.py; sed -n '530,540p' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/backend.py
findings.expected: A plain thickness=15; each backend listed once.
findings.actual: plotly_backend.py:1694: thickness=15 if orientation == 'v' else 15; backend.py backends tuple contains 'TkAgg' at positions 0 and 6

findings.title: plot() Returns section omits HyperAnimation and retains 0.x 'geometry' language for streaming
findings.description: (1) plot.py's Returns section (lines 1213-1216) says 'For animated matplotlib plots a `(fig, animation)` tuple is returned' -- the actual return since QC 2026-07 is a `HyperAnimation` (a tuple subclass with .save/.to_html5_video/.figure, verified: type=HyperAnimation, unpacks=True); the class hyper_animation.py presents as 'the object an animated hyp.plot(...) returns' is never mentioned in plot()'s own docs, so its export methods are undiscoverable from the primary docstring. (2) The stream_window bullet (line 1003) says 'all consumed samples are still retained on the returned geometry' -- 0.x DataGeometry language; 1.0 returns no geometry object.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
out = hyp.plot(np.random.default_rng(3).normal(size=(20, 3)).cumsum(0), animate='spin', duration=1, frame_rate=5, show=False)
print(type(out).__name__, isinstance(out, tuple))
EOF
findings.expected: Returns section names HyperAnimation (noting tuple compatibility); streaming bullet reworded without 'geometry'.
findings.actual: HyperAnimation True -- while plot.py:1213-1216 documents only 'a (fig, animation) tuple' and plot.py:1003 says 'retained on the returned geometry'
